StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterBlockCleared.rationale: Correct slot: C# fires Hook.AfterBlockCleared per creature at CombatManager.cs:500-507, immediately after Creature.AfterTurnStart -> ClearBlock (:492-499) and BEFORE SetupPlayerTurn (:514), and the sim clears and fires at player.py:157-159, the first thing start_turn does and before the energy reset (:163) and the draw (:183). Same owner guard (BlockNextTurnPower.cs:21 vs powers.py:3843), same amount (base.Amount), same props: GainBlock(..., ValueProp.Unpowered, null) at :24 vs props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED at :3847 -- so the regained block ignores Dexterity/Frail and ignores power/no_block and power/unmovable on both sides (cmds.py:145 gates both block families on is_powered_attack). The main report's section 4 item 4 counts this power among the eight siblings that pass UNPOWERED correctly where feel_no_pain and curl_up do not. Remove, not Decrement, on both sides, so it is one-shot regardless of Amount. Shares the slot with power/toric_toughness, which agrees.

guards.what: BlockNextTurnPower.cs:24-25 GainBlock BEFORE Remove; the sim _expires FIRST
guards.rationale: powers.py:3845-3848 calls self._expire() and THEN BlockCmd.apply, the reverse of C#'s order (BlockNextTurnPower.cs:24 then :25). So during the block gain the power is already off the creature in the sim and still on it in the game. No ported listener observes the difference -- the sim's on_block_gained listeners are power/juggernaut (which reads only the target and amount) and relics, none of which reads Blocked Off -- and expiring first has the incidental virtue of making re-entrancy impossible. Kept as a deliberate divergence rather than faithful because it is a real ordering difference; the mirror-image ordering on power/setup_strike's family is recorded the same way. The sim's _expire (powers.py:86-92) pops the power and unregisters it; C#'s PowerCmd.Remove (PowerCmd.cs:287-295) additionally fires power.AfterRemoved, which this power does not implement. Observationally identical, same treatment as the _expire entries in audit/records/power/duplication.json and audit/records/power/flame_barrier.json per binding rule 3.

guards.what: The name mismatch: id block_next_turn, name 'Blocked Off'
guards.rationale: powers.py:3837-3838. Cosmetic; the C# class is BlockNextTurnPower and the displayed title comes from loc data. Recorded because the main report's section 4 item 4 refers to this power as 'Blocked Off' and a reader matching names to ids would otherwise not find it.
The Prolong card (cards/colorless_skills.py:492's `> 0` guard is the one power_cmd's step-6 finding cites as hand-guarding the zero-amount case). No AscensionHelper call in BlockNextTurnPower.cs.
